title: Steps to Make Array Non-decreasing
statement:
You repeatedly apply a step to the integer array `nums`. In a step, every element that has a strictly larger element immediately to its left is deleted. All of these deletions happen together: which elements go is decided on the array as it stands at the start of the step, and then the remaining elements close up in their original order.

Steps continue until the array is non-decreasing. Return how many steps are performed (`0` if `nums` is non-decreasing from the start).
notes:
## Intuition

Simulating the steps works but can take O(n²) time, for example on `[10, 1, 2, 3, ...]`, where only one element disappears per step. Instead, ask for each element in which step it disappears. An element survives forever exactly when nothing before it is larger. Otherwise it is eaten by the nearest larger element on its left, but only after every smaller-or-equal element between them is gone, because those stand in the way. So its step is one more than the latest step among the elements it waits for, and the answer is the largest step of any element.

## Approach

1. Keep a `stack` of pairs `[value, steps]` for elements still able to block later ones; values decrease strictly from bottom to top.
2. For each `value`, pop every entry whose value is `<= value` and keep the largest of their `steps`: those elements must vanish before `value` meets a larger one.
3. If the stack is now empty, nothing on the left is larger, so `steps = 0`. Otherwise `steps` is that largest popped step plus one.
4. Update `answer` and push `[value, steps]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`5` gets `0`. `3` sits under `5`: steps `1`. `4` pops `[3, 1]`, and `5` is larger: steps `2`. The next `4` pops `[4, 2]`: steps `3`, so `answer = 3`. `7` pops everything: `0`. `3` gets `1`; `6` pops it and gets `2`. `11` pops everything: `0`. `8` and `5` each get `1`, and the last `11` empties the stack with `0`. The answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each element is pushed once and popped at most once.
- Space: O(n) for the stack.

## Pitfalls

- Pop entries that are equal as well (`<=`): an equal value on the left does not delete anything, so it only delays.
- An element with nothing larger before it is never deleted, so its steps must be `0`, not the popped maximum plus one.
- The answer is the largest steps value, not the number of deleted elements.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stack` | pairs `[value, steps]` with strictly decreasing values |
| `value` | the current element |
| `steps` | the step in which `value` is deleted (`0` if never) |
| `answer` | the largest `steps` seen so far |

narration.2: The stack holds [value, steps] pairs with strictly decreasing values from bottom to top.
narration.3: answer tracks the latest step in which any element is deleted.
narration.4: Process the elements from left to right.
narration.6: Elements no larger than value cannot delete it; it must wait for them to vanish.
narration.7: Pop one of them and remember the latest step among those that are waited for.
narration.9: If something larger remains on the left, value goes one step after the last blocker; otherwise it is never deleted.
narration.10: Keep the largest step count seen so far.
narration.11: value can now block, or be waited for by, later elements.
narration.13: The number of steps is the largest deletion step.
